title: Photocatalytic degradation of ciprofloxacin using CuFe2O4@methyl cellulose based magnetic nanobiocomposite
author: Tamaddon, Nasiri, et al.

steps.title: Synthesize CuFe2O4@MC
steps.instruction: Prepare the CuFe2O4@methyl cellulose magnetic nanobiocomposite using the described microwave‑assisted method, then characterize the product.

substeps.instruction: Perform microwave‑assisted synthesis as outlined in the method
Characterize the nanocomposite (e.g., X‑ray diffraction, FT‑IR, TEM, magnetic measurements)

steps.title: Compare degradation pathways
steps.instruction: Conduct separate experiments for photolysis, adsorption, and photocatalytic degradation of ciprofloxacin using the synthesized CuFe2O4@MC, and compare their efficiencies.

steps.title: Optimize operational parameters
steps.instruction: Systematically vary operational parameters (such as pH, catalyst dosage, H₂O₂ concentration, irradiation time) to evaluate their effects on ciprofloxacin removal efficiency and determine the optimal conditions.

steps.title: Benchmark against CuFe2O4
steps.instruction: Under the optimized conditions, compare the photocatalytic performance of CuFe2O4@MC with that of bare CuFe2O4.

steps.title: Test on real wastewater
steps.instruction: Apply the optimized photocatalytic system to hospital wastewater samples and measure both ciprofloxacin degradation and chemical oxygen demand (COD) removal.

steps.title: Assess kinetics and reusability
steps.instruction: Determine the photocatalytic removal kinetics of ciprofloxacin and evaluate the reusability and chemical stability of CuFe2O4@MC over multiple cycles.
